scope: Reproducible solver calculations and regression checks, not a new independent NEURON/LFPykit comparison or biological validation. Elapsed times include solver and any uncached conditioning, exclude rendering, and are machine-specific. Output bytes count retained numerical buffers, not peak process memory.

acceptanceCriteria.eventClassification: The qualitative outcome recorded with each curated configuration must hold; active crossings are upward −25 mV with the solver-defined soma detector.
acceptanceCriteria.finite: All retained membrane voltages/currents and recording components must be finite.

cases.title: Human cell · subthreshold current
cases.expectedBehavior: The soma depolarizes without an upward −25 mV crossing. The ideal recording includes neural membrane-current potential and a small separate bath-return contribution.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Human cell · intracellular soma spike
cases.expectedBehavior: One upward soma crossing of −25 mV is detected in this 40 ms experiment. Earlier crossings can occur in the synthetic axon stub. These event criteria do not identify a measured biological initiation site.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Patch clamp · 200 ms current step
cases.expectedBehavior: Nine soma crossings occur during the step. Interspike intervals increase as this modeled cell adapts. Count divided by step duration is 45 Hz, not a constant instantaneous firing rate. These are calculated responses of one fitted cell, not universal biological thresholds.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Patch clamp · 500 ms current step
cases.expectedBehavior: Eighteen soma crossings occur: seventeen during the current step and one just after its offset. Interspike intervals lengthen. Onset, step length, recording length and output interval differ from the 200 ms example; this is not a single-variable comparison. Internal event detection retains full timestep resolution.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Array · local crossings without soma spike
cases.expectedBehavior: Some dendritic compartments cross −25 mV, while the soma does not. The large applied stimulation artifact at the ideal recording contacts is separate from the much smaller neural signal.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Array · calculated soma spike
cases.expectedBehavior: One soma event occurs during this experiment. Strong depolarization and hyperpolarization are consequences of this idealized model and input, not a safe or selective real-brain stimulation prescription.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Placement comparison · unshifted array
cases.expectedBehavior: Local compartments cross −25 mV, but the soma does not. Relative stimulating/recording contact geometry is unchanged, so the applied recording artifact is identical to the shifted-array example; neural signals differ.

crossingCriterion.convention: Upward voltage crossing, linearly interpolated between internal solver steps; earliest crossing is model-dependent

cases.title: Polarity comparison · reversed leading phase
cases.expectedBehavior: One soma event still occurs, but at a different time and with different earlier local crossings. Applied contact potentials reverse sign exactly; the nonlinear neural response need not do so.

cases.title: Recordings · neural, artifact and total
cases.expectedBehavior: Total equals neural plus applied at every retained sample. Applied potential dominates during the pulse and vanishes in the gap and after the pulse; neural potential can persist. Each contact is referenced to infinity, while A−B is their algebraic difference.
